title: Navigating by command line: prompt, PowerShell and shell

videos.script: The server in the cupboard has no desktop. No Start button, no Dock, no icons. When Ana connects to it, she gets a window with one line of text in it and a blinking cursor. Everything she will ever do on that server, she does from there. {{cursor}} It looks less friendly than a desktop and it is, at first. It is also faster once you know it, it works the same over a slow connection from home, and a command can be written down, sent to somebody else, and repeated exactly. A sequence of clicks cannot. {{why}} Every system has one. Linux and macOS have a shell, bash or zsh. Windows has two, the old Command Prompt and PowerShell. They look alike, and they differ in ways that matter the first time you type a path with a space in it. {{three}} In this lesson you will read what a prompt tells you, move around the folders by absolute and relative paths, deal with spaces and with capital letters, do the same things in PowerShell, find help for a command you do not know, and see the one idea that makes PowerShell different from every other shell. {{steps}} The transcripts come from lesson 3's server, in bash, and in PowerShell 7 running on that same machine. The Windows and macOS prompts are shown, not run. {{honest}}
